fields.AN_Notes: Framework derived from a narrative review (Section 1.2). General_Guidance: 'prompts can be intentionally crafted or augmented with instructions to avoid bias' (3.1.3). ICL: example-based prompting with balanced, randomly ordered demographic examples, debiasing and counterfactual data augmentation (3.1.1). Thought_Generation: chain-of-thought with ethical checkpoints (3.1.2). Self_Criticism: final verification step 'Plan verification questions to fact-check this draft' (3.1.2). Object_of_Critique: the 'illusion of transparency' of chain-of-thought explanations (3.1.2). AN_Bias_Axes None: gender and race appear only as enumerated attributes to flip ('flipping attributes like gender or race') and in one cited replacement example, not as an axis the work analyses. AN_Harm_Types None: stereotyping, toxicity and the Gemini misrepresentation incident are cited from other sources or named as tool targets, the work's own argument establishes no harm mechanism. Mitigation stays Proposed, no own or synthesised completed assessment with a reported result. AN_Task None: recruitment, performance reviews and legal analysis are illustrations of a general framework. AN_Theory_Reference No: value-sensitive design is named as an aligned responsibility-by-design approach, not as a frame for bias.

fields.AN_Notes: Evaluated intervention: CCSV (collective critiques plus self-voting over multiple decodes) applied in-context to Flan-PaLM 540B, compared with 0-shot IF, 0-shot CoT, 5-shot, 5-shot CoT and 5-shot CAI baselines; the work's own experiment reports large entropy and max-gap gains and human side-by-side preference (Sections 5.1, 6). Self_Criticism and Ensembling are the CCSV critique and voting steps; ICL and Thought_Generation are the few-shot and CoT conditions; General_Guidance is the 0-shot IF condition 'Instruction: Write AI model's response to the user question such that it has diversity'. Language_Culture: the cultural-diversity task rated by humans (Section 6.2). Gender categories are male, female and other from a knowledge graph; the work states that 'other' is not an ideal stand-in for genders beyond male and female, so the analysis is coded Binary_Categorical and the definition Implicit_Only. Fine-tuning with CCSV-generated data is named only as future work and not coded as In_Training. Identity: corpus and text titles differ, see identity_check.

fields.AN_Notes: Narrative review article. Bias axes are the worked examples of Sections 4.1 and 4.1.1: child-abuse risk scores over-representing families from certain ethnic backgrounds (Race_Ethnicity), housing-voucher algorithms favouring affluent neighbourhoods (Socioeconomic), chatbots designed for English-speaking users (Language_Culture). Gender appears only in the enumeration 'racial, gender, or socio-economic disparities' and is not coded. Indirect_Discrimination: the review's own argument that models trained on historical data replicate past disparities and affect access to services, child welfare interventions and support (allocation through biased historical data, not through the attribute itself). The language exclusion of chatbots is only a cited case and is not coded as a harm type. Mitigation proposals: diverse and inclusive datasets (Pre_Processing); auditing, involvement of social workers and community members, transparency, training (Organisational_Process); none is assessed. Tasks: predictive risk assessment (Case_Assessment_Decision_Support), mental-health chatbots (Counselling_Client_Communication), NLP summaries of case notes and automated case documentation (Documentation_Recording). Source quality: several in-text citations do not match the reference list, e.g. 'Baker et al., 2021' cited for NLP documentation while reference [3] is a review of AI in net-zero building design, and 'Dastidar et al., 2019' next to a reference list that also holds 'Dastin, J. (2018)'; flagged for the domain experts, the publication type itself is a journal review article.

fields.AN_Notes: Intervention: an AI-bias training module inside co-creation workshops with marginalised groups (women at risk of social exclusion, ethnic minorities, migrants, young people, LGBTQI+ early career researchers) for the MAMMOth bias toolkit. Outcome reported only as facilitator and participant reflections, no completed assessment of an effect on AI bias, hence Demonstrated. Bias axes: gender through the training examples added by DAF (generative AI answers on fathers and mothers, gendered job endings in Google Translate); religion and physical appearance through the facial-attribute ranking in the identity-verification use case (hijabs and turbans, piercings and tattoos). The enumeration 'gender, age, ethnic origin, and sexual orientation' and the participant view that white males benefit most from AI credit scoring are not coded. Indirect_Discrimination: postal codes as proxy of race in the toolkit's object; Stereotyping: the gender-role examples demonstrated in the training. Other_Task: AI uses discussed are bank loan decisions, biometric identity verification and academic citation search, outside social work. Gender is treated through examples only, without a stated or recognisable understanding of the work's own, hence Absent and Unclear. Theory reference: critical perspectives on participatory design (power relations, 'box-ticking', ethics-washing) frame the treatment of AI bias and training; the line between a framing tradition and a methodological label is a borderline case.
